jobs.description: Role: Senior Data Engineer    Location: DFYNE HQ, 1 Forrest Gate, Uddingston, G71 5PG    Work Location: Onsite    About You:   Are you the kind of Data Engineer who enjoys being the person everyone relies on when data matters most? Do you thrive on building reliable pipelines, improving data quality and ensuring critical business decisions are driven by trusted information? Are you as comfortable writing complex SQL as you are building automated monitoring, troubleshooting failures and improving data architecture? If you enjoy ownership and want to have a direct impact on how a fast-growing business operates, DFYNE could be exactly where you belong.   About DFYNE:   A picture paints a thousand words… and we’re sure you don’t want to sit here reading a corporate essay about who we are. Honestly, how can you really get under the skin of DFYNE from a few lines on a screen? So instead, go have a look for yourself, see what we’re about, what we stand for, and why people love us: www.dfyne.com.   About the role — DFYNE Your Career:   Before I tell you more about the role, let me introduce myself. I’m Bruce, Head of Development at DFYNE, and I’m looking for our first dedicated Senior Data Engineer. This role will own the DFYNE data warehouse, helping ensure the data that powers finance reporting, forecasting, inventory management and operational decision-making remains accurate, reliable and available. You’ll take ownership of BigQuery pipelines, transformation layers, exports and integrations while working closely with teams across the business. This is a hands-on role where you’ll help define data engineering standards, improve data reliability and build the foundation of DFYNE’s future data capability.   Attitude:   • Ownership mentality • Builder mindset • Commercial awareness • Problem-solving mindset • Continuous improvement   Key Responsibilities:   • Own the performance, reliability, security and ongoing development of DFYNE’s BigQuery data warehouse and associated data pipelines. • Design, build and maintain scalable ingestion and transformation processes. • Implement data quality monitoring, validation and automated alerting. • Define data contracts with business stakeholders and system owners. • Improve reliability, accuracy and freshness of business-critical data. • Lead investigation and resolution of data incidents, ensuring root causes are identified and permanently addressed. • Support ERP, finance, forecasting and operational reporting requirements. • Build and maintain integrations for fulfilment and logistics platforms. • Identify and resolve data quality issues and pipeline failures. • Contribute to data architecture, governance and engineering standards. • Collaborate closely with Finance, Operations and Engineering teams. • Support reporting, analytics and business intelligence initiatives. • Drive continuous improvement across DFYNE’s data platform.   Skills & Experience:   • 5+ years of commercial Data Engineering experience. • Expert SQL skills and strong Python development experience. • Hands-on BigQuery experience or equivalent cloud data warehouse technologies. • Experience with dbt, Dataform or similar transformation frameworks. • Experience building and operating production data pipelines. • Experience implementing monitoring, testing and alerting for data systems. • Strong understanding of data quality, governance and reliability. • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills. • Experience supporting finance, ERP or operational reporting environments. • Ability to translate business requirements into scalable data solutions.   Nice to Have:   • Google Cloud Platform certifications. • Logistics, fulfilment or e-commerce experience. • Terraform and Infrastructure as Code experience. • Experience with modern analytics and reporting tools. • Experience scaling data platforms in high-growth businesses.   So, what’s in it for you?:   If you’ve made it this far down without being put off, brilliant. I’d genuinely love to hear from you. Beyond joining a work family and a genuinely great place to build your career, you’ll become DFYNE’s first dedicated Data Engineer and help shape the future of data within one of the UK’s fastest-growing companies. You’ll work on a modern data platform supporting finance, forecasting, ERP and operational decision-making while having genuine ownership and influence from day one.   You’ll be part of a high challenge; high reward culture.    What will aid a successful application with DFYNE:   • Cover letter • Completed questionnaire   Salary starting from £65k per year. jobs.title: Head of Technology
jobs.description: We are hiring a  Head of Technology  for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.    Original job posting link     About  garden3d    We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.  Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy & Gagosian.  Weâre the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone & Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.  We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.   Sanctuary Computer - Development   At   Sanctuary Computer   weâre building a different type of technology shop â one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.  Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.   XXIX - Design   When we started   XXIX   in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and weâve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.  Weâre building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.   Index - Community     Index   is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.  We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.    garden3d TK  â Media   At garden3d, weâre in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.  We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.  Plus, our partner organizations    Lightphone     Mill     IngredientAI    â°ï¸ The Head of Technology Role  The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.  You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.  This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.  This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.  They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.  They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.   Responsibilities & Mandates   ï¸  Systems that hold up   We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.   All in on agentic development   The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.   Practical engineering   We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.   Code quality at Sanctuary Computer   Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.   Hiring and empowering the very best   They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.   Estimation, scoping and delivery   They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.   The technical voice in new business   Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.   Hardware sense   We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.   The garden3d technology story   Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.   Culture   They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off  Â  Special Projects   In addition to day to day responsibilities, hereâs an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years â   Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts  Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from  Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do  Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio  Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products  Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed   Qualifications  This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:   Must have:    12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company  Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products  A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native  A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure  All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase  Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it  Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients  A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them  Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)    Nice-to-have:    A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products  Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)  Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role  Open source projects they've started or maintained  Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams  Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company  A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring  Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality   Who you are  The person weâre looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. Theyâre flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work âsmartâ by carefully managing their workflow and team.  How we interview  After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.  From there, weâll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where weâre going as a business.  For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.  Compensation   This is a permanent leadership role.  If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.  We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between  $110 - $175  p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.  At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators.  â  How we work:   We believe that thereâs a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops:     Transparency & Ownership : Â We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. Weâre proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.    150% Carbon Negative :  Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same.  We have been certified climate neutral since 2021 .    Strong Morals :  Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).   Async & Decentralized:  We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.   Remote Friendly: Â Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.   Ideas & Products: Â In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?   â Read more on our  Substack, over here .   How to apply   Weâre excited to hear from you! â¤   Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity.  Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are. 
 The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking. 
 This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer. 
 We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it. 
 If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you. 
 What Work Looks Like 
 You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable. 
 Every day 
 
 Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it. 
 Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution. 
 Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform. 
 
 Delighting customers 
 
 Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success. 
 Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked. 
 Share customer feedback with the team, ask happy customers for reviews and case studies, and watch NPS for testimonial candidates. 
 
 Making support smarter with AI 
 
 Improve the AI support agent. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off. 
 Write and maintain automated tests, built with AI, that try to break staging before customers do. 
 Use the MCP connections we have in place (Helpscout, GitHub, Postmark, and others) to get an accurate picture of support and find the next thing worth improving. 
 
 Keeping the product solid 
 
 Gatekeep releases. New fixes and features land on staging every week. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected. 
 Report bugs as GitHub issues with everything the developer needs: steps to reproduce, screenshots or a Loom, and any GraphQL or console errors. 
 Captain red alerts. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice. 
 
 Running the week 
 
 Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated. 
 Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps. 
 
 Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude. 
 Who You Are 
 
 You build rapport fast. You are warm, positive, and relatable in writing and on calls. 
 You are a good communicator. Externally, you can show warmth, empathy and care. Internally, you are able to communicate clearly and concisely about important things. 
 You can operate with minimal instructions. You understand a short brief without every detail spelled out. You can prioritize well (especially when you have a lot on your plate), and get things done without hand-holding. 
 You are comfortable on video. You are natural on live calls with Zoom and Meet, and on recorded video through tools like Loom. 
 Your teammates can always count on you. You say what you'll do and you do what you said. 
 You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity. 
 You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results. 
 You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack. 
 Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive. 
 Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are. 
 
 A Plus If You Have 
 
 Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role. 
 Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps. 
 Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client. 
 Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report. 
 An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment. 
 
 How We Work Together 
 You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer. 
 Working with the founder can be intense. Here is what that looks like in practice: 
 
 Replies are short and can come across as harsh. If something written lands badly or isn't clear, ask. 
 Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt. 
 Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked. 
 The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on. 
 The team often thinks fast and interrupts each other when discussing ideas. If that would bother you, this role probably isn't for you. 
 
 This role suits someone with high emotional intelligence, who doesn't take things personally, asks when something is unclear, and keeps many things moving at once. 
 Your schedule can be flexible. If you have a martial arts class every Thursday at 3 pm, go and make up the time later. In return, on the rare occasion the team needs your help on a weekend, we ask you to be flexible too. 
 Benefits 
 
 Contract type: full-time or part-time 
 Compensation: $2,500 to $4,000 USD per month, depending on experience and location. US-based hires will work as independent contractors (1099). 
 Start date: negotiable

Develop relationships across complex buying groups, including CIOs, CTOs, transformation leaders, enterprise architects, process owners, procurement, security, legal, and executive sponsors.    Lead the full enterprise sales cycle: discovery, qualification, value engineering, technical evaluation, business case, procurement, commercial negotiation, and close.    Apply MEDDICC consistently to create deal clarity, strengthen qualification, identify gaps early, and improve forecast reliability.    Build business cases connected to public-sector outcomes such as service quality, operational efficiency, transparency, resilience, compliance, and cost control. Developa partner-first motion with relevant global system integrators, regional partners, and public-sector specialists.    Expand successful customer relationships by identifying adjacent processes, departments, agencies, and use cases after the initial land. Align with internal stakeholders on territory priorities, account ownership, partner coverage, and available sales resources. Establish a repeatable operating cadence for pipeline creation, deal inspection, forecasting, and cross-functional account-team collaboration.     First 90 days     Complete strategic account plans for the highest-priority government accounts, including business priorities, buying groups, whitespace, partners, competition, and next actions.    Create qualified pipeline through a balanced mix of net-new opportunities, partner-sourced activity, executive introductions, and expansion plays.    Develop a strong network of relevant government and ecosystem stakeholders, with clear relationship and meeting objectives.    Demonstrate consistent MEDDICC qualification and accurate Salesforce hygiene across active opportunities.    Identify the most relevant public-sector use cases and value narratives for Camunda’s Dutch market development.     First 180 days and beyond     Establish a credible, repeatable pipeline engine for the Dutch Government market.    Progress strategic opportunities through well-defined qualification, value validation, technical evaluation, procurement, and commercial stages.    Win new government logos and create expansion paths into additional departments, agencies, or processes.    Build trusted relationships with executive sponsors and public-sector ecosystem partners.    Contribute actionable market insight that improves Camunda’s positioning, messaging, partner strategy, and investment decisions in the Netherlands.    Deliver against quota while protecting long-term customer value, adoption, and expansion potential.    What you will bring   Must-haves     5+ years of success in a quota-carrying enterprise software or SaaS Account Executive role, owning complex deals end to end.    Demonstrated experience selling into the Dutch Government or another highly regulated public-sector environment, with a clear understanding of formal procurement, security, legal, and governance requirements.    A track record of creating pipeline through proactive outbound activity and converting multi-stakeholder opportunities into material, preferably multi-year, contracts.    Strong command of MEDDICC or a comparable enterprise sales methodology, with the discipline to qualify rigorously, manage mutual action plans, and forecast accurately.    Executive presence and communication skills in Dutch and English, with the ability to connect operational problems to strategic, financial, and citizen-impact outcomes.    A collaborative, customer-focused, and resilient approach aligned with Camunda’s FAITH values and global-first way of working.     Nice-to-haves     Experience selling process automation, workflow, orchestration, integration, business transformation, or adjacent enterprise technology.    Existing relationships across Dutch ministries, executive agencies, municipalities, provinces, public-service organizations, or government-focused partners.    Experience working with global system integrators, regional implementation partners, or public-sector framework agreements.    Familiarity with Camunda, BPMN, DMN, process orchestration, cloud platforms, or agentic automation.    Experience creating quantified value cases for service modernization, compliance, operational resilience, or cost reduction. The role offers the chance to work at the intersection of public-sector transformation, enterprise technology, process orchestration, and the next generation of agentic automation. jobs.title: Sales Development Representative
jobs.description: Über uns  Lupa entwickelt ein Produkt, das eine völlig neue Kategorie schafft und das es in der Branche so noch nicht gegeben hat.  Wir sind das KI-native Betriebssystem für Tierarztpraxen und Tierhalter. Unsere intelligente All-in-one-Plattform ersetzt die fragmentierten, umständlichen Systeme, mit denen Tierarztpraxen seit Jahren arbeiten müssen. Sie vereint Terminplanung, Kundenkommunikation, klinische Dokumentation und KI-gestützte Behandlungsempfehlungen. Praxen arbeiten dadurch effizienter, Tierärzte können sich wieder auf das konzentrieren, was sie lieben, und Tierhalter sind enger mit der Gesundheit ihrer Tiere verbunden als je zuvor.  Unsere Erfolge sprechen für sich: 2023 gegründet, sind wir heute Marktführer in Großbritannien, gehören zu den 100 führenden KI-Start-ups Europas und sind in zwölf Monaten um das Zehnfache gewachsen. Unser Team zählt inzwischen 70 Mitarbeitende und wächst schnell weiter. Jetzt expandieren wir mit voller Kraft in die USA und nach Europa. Wir haben 25 Millionen US-Dollar an Finanzierung erhalten, betreuen mehr als 2,5 Millionen Haustiere auf unserer Plattform und haben ein lebendiges Büro in München. Außergewöhnliche Talente von Unternehmen wie Palantir, Google, DeepMind, BCG, Meta und AWS sind bereits Teil unseres Teams, und wir stehen erst am Anfang.  Dies ist die seltene Gelegenheit, genau zum richtigen Zeitpunkt Teil eines rasant wachsenden Unternehmens zu werden. Deshalb suchen wir außergewöhnliche Menschen, die dieses Wachstum aktiv mitgestalten möchten.   In dieser Rolle wirst du:     Die Outbound-Akquise für Tierarztpraxen und Tierkliniken verantworten. Diese Pipeline baust du selbst auf    Hochwertige Leads identifizieren, recherchieren und per Kaltakquise über Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn ansprechen    Interessenten qualifizieren und Termine für unsere Account Executives vereinbaren, inklusive einer Übergabe mit allem relevanten Kontext    Ein tiefes Verständnis für das Produkt, die Kunden und den Markt von Lupa aufbauen, damit deine Ansprache beratend ist und nicht nach Skript klingt    Eng mit Marketing und Produkt zusammenarbeiten, um Messaging und Positionierung auf Basis deiner Erfahrungen aus der Praxis zu schärfen    Die Pipelinedaten im CRM korrekt und aktuell halten, denn unser Team arbeitet mit sauberen Daten    Erkenntnisse aus deinen Gesprächen mit Interessenten an das Team weitergeben und so unsere Go-to-Market-Strategie und Produktentwicklung mitgestalten     Dein Hintergrund könnte wie folgt aussehen:     Fundierte Vertriebserfahrung als SDR, BDR oder in einer anderen Outbound-Rolle. Erfahrung in B2B SaaS oder Tech ist von Vorteil, aber auch andere Branchen sind willkommen!    Fließende Deutschkenntnisse sind ein Muss    Bereitschaft, vor Ort in unserem Büro in München zu arbeiten    Du bist sicher in der Akquise per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn und gehst dabei beratend vor    Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsstärke: Du kannst den Mehrwert eines Produkts klar vermitteln, sowohl gegenüber medizinischem Fachpersonal als auch gegenüber nicht technischen Ansprechpartnern    Sehr gute Organisation und hohe Eigenmotivation: Du behältst mehrere Interessenten und Pipelines gleichzeitig im Blick, ohne an Schwung zu verlieren    Erfahrung mit einem CRM und ein datengetriebener Ansatz zur Verbesserung deiner Outreach-Ergebnisse sind von Vorteil    Erfahrung im Vertrieb von Vertical SaaS oder im Umfeld professioneller Dienstleistungen ist von Vorteil     Als Person:     Interessierst du dich ehrlich für die Herausforderungen deiner Kunden und willst sie lösen, anstatt nur eine Anrufquote zu erfüllen    Bist du hungrig auf Wachstum und bereit, alles für deinen Erfolg zu geben    Bist du belastbar: Absagen bringen dich nicht aus der Ruhe, sie machen dich besser    Möchtest du dich in eine Closing-Rolle entwickeln und siehst die SDR-Position als Sprungbrett, nicht als Endstation    Freust du dich darauf, vor Ort in unserem Büro in München zu arbeiten, mit gelegentlichen Reisen zu unserem Hauptsitz in London    Arbeitest du gerne mit Menschen, die freundlich, ambitioniert und pragmatisch sind    Liebst du Tiere? Das ist ein Bonus, denn du verkaufst an Menschen, die ihr Berufsleben den Tieren gewidmet haben     Wie sieht Erfolg nach sechs Monaten aus?     Du vereinbarst kontinuierlich qualifizierte Termine, und deine Pipeline ist eine, mit der unsere Account Executives wirklich gerne arbeiten    Du kennst Produkt, Markt und Kunden so gut, dass du Discovery Calls eigenständig führen kannst    Du prägst bereits, wie das Team über Outbound denkt. Deine Erkenntnisse aus der Praxis verändern, wie wir in den Markt gehen    Find  Jobs in Germany  on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Senior Partner Manager - DACH
jobs.description: About the Role   As our  Senior Partner Manager DACH , you'll own and grow Tellent's partner ecosystem across the DACH market. You'll inherit an established network of reseller and referral partners, including a group of key strategic partners with significant growth potential — and your role is to turn that foundation into a stronger, more predictable source of pipeline and revenue.  You'll build trusted relationships with key partners, create joint growth plans, identify whitespace opportunities across their customer base, and hold partners accountable for execution. At the same time, you'll identify and recruit new high-potential partners, particularly within the HR ecosystem. This is a senior individual contributor role: you'll operate with significant ownership, treating the DACH partner business almost like your own business and bringing a clear point of view on where the market can grow.  You will report to the  VP Partnerships .     Your 12-Month Journey      During the first 3 months:  You build a strong understanding of the DACH partner ecosystem, establish relationships with key partners and Sales stakeholders, and define a clear plan for where to focus your time and investment.     Within 6 months:  You're independently managing the partner portfolio, driving joint business plans with key partners, generating quality pipeline, and identifying new partner opportunities.     After 1 year:  You're driving predictable partner-sourced pipeline and revenue across DACH, growing the strategic partner portfolio, and expanding the ecosystem with new partners that contribute meaningful business.       What You'll Be Doing      Strategic Partner Management:  Own and grow Tellent's most impactful DACH partner relationships, building long-term relationships and joint business plans focused on mutual growth.     Partner Performance:  Monitor partner health, pipeline and revenue performance, identify risks early, and hold partners accountable to agreed activities and results.     Commercial Growth:  Generate partner-sourced pipeline and revenue, improve opportunity quality and conversion, and ensure strong collaboration with Sales throughout the deal cycle.     Account & Whitespace Planning:  Work side by side with strategic partners to analyse their customer base, identify whitespace opportunities and build plans to generate new business together.     Partner Acquisition:  Identify, qualify and recruit high-potential new partners, particularly across the HR ecosystem, assessing them based on strategic fit and revenue potential.     Activation & Enablement:  Ensure new and existing partners are effectively enabled on Tellent, our products, ICP and sales approach, and turn partnerships into active commercial relationships.     Market Development:  Bring a strong point of view on the DACH market, identifying opportunities beyond the existing partner ecosystem and translating ideas into concrete execution.     Collaboration:  Work closely with Sales, particularly the DACH Sales team, as well as Marketing and other Partnerships colleagues to improve deal execution, campaigns, enablement and pipeline quality.     Operational Excellence:  Identify recurring friction in the partner GTM motion and contribute to improving playbooks, cadences, partner planning and ways of working across the wider Partnerships team.       What You Bring      Partnership Experience:  Several years of experience in a partner, channel or business development role, with a proven track record of building and growing strategic partner relationships.     DACH Market Expertise:  Strong understanding of the German market and ideally an established network of relevant DACH partners.     SaaS Experience:  Experience in B2B SaaS, ideally within HR tech or an adjacent mid-market/SMB environment.     Commercial Skill:  Strong understanding of pipeline generation, forecasting, partner planning and commercial performance, with experience in reseller and/or referral models.     Strategic Thinking:  Able to assess a partner portfolio, identify where the biggest opportunities are, and make clear decisions about where to invest time and resources.     Execution:  You don't just have ideas — you turn them into structured plans, actions and measurable results.     Entrepreneurial Mindset:  You take ownership of the DACH partner business as if it were your own, proactively looking for opportunities and challenging existing assumptions.     Relationship Building:  Strong at building trusted relationships while also being comfortable setting expectations, challenging partners and addressing underperformance.     Self-Management:  Highly organised and able to manage a broad portfolio, prioritising time effectively across partners, Sales and new opportunities.     Communication:  Professional fluency in German and English, comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders and operating across cross-functional teams.     Travel:  Comfortable travelling regularly across Germany to build and maintain strong in-person partner relationships.       What We Offer     Flexible working in the Cologne area as we continue building our local team presence    Diverse and international team environment    €1,500 annual learning budget    Pension scheme & wellness/fitness benefits    Country-specific holiday policies apply    Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year    Apple MacBook and all the tools you need to succeed    Home office budget and allowance       About Tellent   Tellent is a leading Talent Management Suite designed to empower HR & People teams across the entire employee journey. Our all-in-one platform combines an Applicant Tracking System ( Tellent Recruitee ), an intuitive HRIS ( Tellent HR ), and powerful Performance Management software ( Tellent Grow ).  With 250+ team members globally, 7,000+ customers in 100+ countries, and a growing ecosystem of 500+ partners, we help organizations attract, grow, and retain top talent — and we’re just getting started. Deutschkenntnisse auf muttersprachlichem Niveau sowie fließende Englischkenntnisse.      Präsentations- und Argumentationsfähigkeit sowie ausgeprägte Networking-Kompetenzen. Cross-Stack Engineering:  Design integration concepts, CAD models, electrical circuits and system integration and bring together sensors, enclosures, calibration, compute, mechanisms, power electronics, controls, networking, autonomy software, and operator workflows. Own readiness checks across calibration, software flashing, networking, sensors, and pre-mission setup. Make readiness measurable and repeatable.     Field Deployment & End-User Interface:  Install, configure, maintain, and support SE3 systems at test ranges, customer sites, partner demonstrations, exercises, and real-world deployments. You don’t wait for perfect information. You create clarity, iterate fast, and prefer finding and fixing root causes over applying patches.    You hold a B.Sc., M.Sc. or similar degree in Robotics, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Embedded Systems, Mechatronics, or a related field. You are proficient in using CAD software, creating wiring diagrams, building electromechanic prototypes and defining and executing test campaigns across hardware disciplines.    You are familiar with soldering, crimping, using multimeters, oscilloscopes, serial consoles, or other lab and field equipment, with at least basic experience in command line, data analysis tools and Linux usage.    You are proactive, hands-on and able to find effective solutions also under the constraints of field-campaigns and willing to travel and deploy across Europe.    You enjoy working directly with partners, operators, and end users. You can explain technical problems clearly, build trust in stressful situations, and represent SE3 professionally outside the lab.    You speak fluent English; German is a strong plus. A driving license is required. Given the nature of SE3’s work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to work on defence-related projects and, where required, obtain the relevant security clearance.           Especially Valued Bonus Skills     Specific knowledge in UAVs, PX4, ArduPilot, QGroundControl, Mission Planner, MAVLink, flight log analysis, mission planning, and airspace coordination.    Proficiency in PCBA and electronics circuit design and prototyping, especially targeting high-speed data interfaces and sensors    Experience with development on ROS2, Docker, Linux, edge compute devices, C++/Python, Bash, Git, or deployment automation.    Experience with networking and radio systems, including WiFi networks, LTE/5G modems, VPNs, telemetry links, antenna placement, RF interference, tactical communication links, and debugging connectivity issues in the field.    Experience with perception or measurement systems, camera/IMU calibration, sensor synchronization, image processing, or mission autonomy.    Skills interpreting sensor data, robot logs, flight logs, frequency-domain data, vibration issues, EMI issues, thermal issues, or intermittent hardware failures.    Experience with environmental testing such as vibration, thermal, ingress protection, EMI/EMC, or MIL-STD-style qualification workflows. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer
jobs.description:
A World-Changing Company   
   
 Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.      The Role  
   
 Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations, and projects often start with an open ended question like “Why are we delaying so many flights?” or “How can we better identify instances of money laundering?” As an FDSE, you’ll apply your problem solving ability, creativity, and technical skills to help organizations use their data to drive a real impact in the world. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.   As an FDSE, your responsibilities look similar to those of a startup CTO: you’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer executives, or establishing strategy for your team.   Whether you aspire to be an entrepreneur or an engineering leader, we believe Palantir is the best place — with the best colleagues — to learn how. You’ll learn how to unpack a problem and understand the costs and consequences of its solution. You’ll learn new technologies and languages, and even develop them yourself. You’ll work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop.   Core Responsibilities  
 Impact: We take on meaningful and challenging projects that change the world for the better. 
 Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter. 
 Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on site, to understand and solve their problems. 
 Trust: We trust each other to effectively manage time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves. 
 Growth: We encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge. 
 Learning: We often face entirely novel problems where we need to pick up a lot of new knowledge and learn how to use it to make progress. We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers. 
  What We Value  
 Strong engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Data Science. 
 A highly analytical mindset and eagerness to solve technical problems with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools. 
 Experience or interest in working with and using large scale data to solve valuable business problems. 
 Strong coder with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar. 
 Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals, and comfortable working in a rapidly changing environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users. 
 Ability to continuously learn, work independently, and make decisions with minimal supervision. 
 Willingness and interest to travel as needed to client sites. Ability to travel 25-50% preferred, but may vary by team and location. 
  What We Require  
 Fluency in German 
 Security clearance or the ability to obtain a clearance. 
   Life at Palantir   
   
 We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at  Life at Palantir  and note that our offerings may vary by region. 
   
 In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office. 
   
 If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process ,  please   and let us know how we can help. 
   
  Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US  FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . jobs.title: Product Manager – Operations Systems (m/f/x)
jobs.description: Ready to become part of the most important mission on this planet?    We are rebuy, pioneers in the sustainable reuse of electronics and media, and we are looking for you! The systems that run this flow are the focus of this team, and the users are the hundreds of colleagues in our operations teams.     You will own the tools and services behind inbound processing, grading and quality control, fulfillment, and returns. Your users are warehouse operators, graders, pickers, and operations leads. Your customers are, in the end, every rebuy buyer and seller who relies on the condition and delivery promise we make.      For this role we need someone who is genuinely detail-oriented, who reads the data before forming an opinion, who understands systems and data flows end-to-end, and who can translate operational reality into precise requirements and measurable outcomes.      As a Product Manager you work hand in hand with operations leadership, team leads, engineering, and data to deliver measurable efficiency and quality improvements. You will spend time on the floor with the people who use your products, translate their goals and constraints into a roadmap you own, build the business case with unit economics together with operations and finance, and negotiate scope and timing with engineering. Improvements are co-created with the people who run the operation, not handed to them. needs early       Drive data-backed decisions:    Analyze KPIs, pull data, avoid measurement traps, and connect feature changes to unit economics improvements       Write precise requirements:    Specify business rules, edge cases, data models, state transitions, integrations, and failure modes for engineering       Ship iteratively without disruption:    Sequence releases safely using pilots, feature flags, parallel runs, change management, and pre-defined metrics       Collaborate across teams:    Engage in technical discussions and manage scope, time, and urgency trade-offs with tech and ops leads       Build stakeholder buy-in:    Align ops, CS, tech, finance, and leadership on shared metrics via clear written communication         Requirements:       3+ years of experience in effects of a change      Experience collaborating with engineering on technical decisions, including integrations and data migrations, and negotiating scope and time-to-market trade-offs      Clear, structured communication skills, written and verbal, with the ability to build buy-in with operations team leads, engineering, and product leadership      Comfort using AI tools (e.g., Claude, Copilot) to accelerate daily work such as analysis, writing, and prototyping      Fluency in English and German        Location:     Berlin    Hybrid model (Must be willing to have regular presence at   About Tensordyne   
 Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team.  At Tensordyne, we are at the forefront of cutting-edge AI hardware and software solutions. To keep pace in this dynamic, interdisciplinary field, we are seeking a  Working Student in ML Compiler Engineering  to contribute to the development of compilers for our custom ASICs. 
 This role offers an exciting opportunity to gain hands-on experience in full-stack compiler engineering while working alongside a team of experts in a fast-paced, innovative environment. If you are passionate about machine learning compilers, numerical programming, and performance optimization, we'd love to hear from you! 
 As a working student, you'll gain valuable experience in a dynamic and innovative environment that thrives on curiosity and collaboration. This part-time role (20 hours per week) is based on-site at our Munich office..

jobs.title: Account Executive, Deployments
jobs.description: Accelerating embodied AGI.   The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.  microagi is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab.  Atlas  captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line.  Shift  records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.  We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.  Most sales roles hand you a territory, a playbook and a quota. This one hands you a market that does not exist yet. We are looking for a builder: someone who would rather create a market than inherit one. Our first enterprise customers are live and the signal is clear. Everything after that is yours to build.  Putting physical AI onto a production line is not a software sale. It reaches the plant manager, the COO, the works council, safety and compliance, IT, procurement, and often the CEO. Deals take time, run through site visits and technical assessments, and are won on trust. Your job is to close our first deals in DACH and turn them into a market we own.     We look for ownership, high agency and low ego, someone who wants to shape both our customer base, shape how we sell and succeed.    What You Will Do    Close our first enterprise deals in DACH. Own each one end to end, from first conversation to signed contract.    Run the full cycle: discovery, NDAs, use cases and footage, site visits, and a technical deployment assessment covering hardware, data, investment and timeline.    Seek the truth on every deal. Find out what Atlas can and cannot do on each customer’s line, say it plainly, and never sell what we cannot deliver, even when it costs the deal.    Navigate the whole buying group: plant managers, COOs, works councils, safety and compliance, procurement, and the board. Bring each of them along.    Build your own pipeline. Find the industrial champions in your market and get in the room.    Develop the playbook as you go: who we sell to, how we price, what wins and what does not. The next ten sellers will run on what you build.    Take what you learn on the floor back to product, research and deployment.      Requirements    A track record of building, wherever you earned it: a market, a team, a company, a product line. Something that exists because you made it.    Enterprise sales experience. You have closed long, complex deals with many stakeholders, and you know how to keep them moving when they stall.    At your best in ambiguity. No map, no precedent, no one to ask.    You sell a vision and people trust you with it. Honest, likeable, low ego, high standards.    Willing to get your hands dirty. You build the account lists, write the proposals, and go to site yourself.    Fluent German and English.    Based in Munich, in the office, with regular travel to customer sites.      Nice to Have    You have sold to operations buyers: plant or site managers, COOs, heads of manufacturing or logistics.    You have run pilots, POCs, or hardware-plus-software deals.    You have been early somewhere: founding AE, first sales hire, or early Head of Sales.    A background in operations consulting, VC, or as a founder.    Who Will Thrive at microagi  Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:     Mission and vision:  you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.     Intensity:  you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.     Entrepreneurial:  you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.     Raw IQ:  you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.     This is for you if:     You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.    You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.    You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.     This is not for you if:     You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.    You would forward output you cannot explain.    "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.    How We Hire  We read every application and reply within five working days.     Talent Screen  (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.     Technical or Functional Interview  (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.     Your Work  (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.     Leadership  (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.     Coworking Day  (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.    Then a decision, usually within a few days.  Pay Transparency  Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.  What We Offer     Agency:  real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.     Freedom:  to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.     A seat on a rocketship:  one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.     Free food and drinks  in the office.    Equal Opportunity  microagi welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.  Find  Jobs in Germany  on Arbeitnow

jobs.description: About the Team   The OpenAI for Government AI Architect team partners with public sector organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with government agencies, public institutions, and partner organizations serving the government to identify where AI can advance critical missions, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, Global Affairs, and specialist delivery teams to help public sector customers adopt advanced AI responsibly and effectively.   About the Role   As an AI Architect, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will shape each customer's AI strategy and guide their journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable mission impact.  You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate mission priorities into a focused use-case portfolio, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable customer value. The Account Director leads the overall account strategy and relationship, while you lead the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production impact.  You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, and partners to provide deeper expertise and execute work where needed. This role calls for strong public sector fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy and hands-on technical conversations.  This role is based in Munich or London. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.   In this role, you will:     Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of public sector customers and pre-sales prospects.    Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, and expansion opportunities.    Lead discovery with agency leaders, mission owners, executives, and technical teams to identify, qualify, and prioritize use cases tied to meaningful mission and operational outcomes.    Develop clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.    Guide customers through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, building confidence in both the solution and its path to production.    Help customers navigate the security, compliance, governance, and deployment requirements that shape AI adoption in the public sector.    Maintain a focused use-case portfolio with clear decision criteria, ownership, blockers, success measures, delivery needs, and adoption plans.    Develop trusted relationships and technical champions across CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, Chief Data and AI Officers, program leaders, engineering teams, and other customer stakeholders.    Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, security, product and domain specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.    Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged. Apply public sector and mission expertise to recognize repeatable patterns, sharpen customer priorities, and identify relevant expansion opportunities.    Share customer insights with Product, Engineering, and Research, translating field learnings into better products, architecture guidance, and reusable practices.     You might thrive in this role if you:     Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.    Have guided complex organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable impact.    Have experience working with government agencies, public institutions, or government contractors and understand how mission priorities, security, compliance, governance, and procurement considerations shape technology adoption.    Build credibility with senior technical and government leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers and program teams.    Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.    Understand modern AI systems, frontier models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, and enterprise AI workflows.    Can prototype, explain technical tradeoffs, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.    Exercise sound judgment about when to go deep personally, when to involve specialists, and how to establish clear handoffs and ownership.    Have experience developing technical account plans, prioritizing complex customer portfolios, and connecting adoption to measurable outcomes.    Bring meaningful expertise in a relevant public sector mission or customer segment.    Communicate clearly and can turn ambiguity into a practical technical narrative, executive decision, or action plan.    Work collaboratively across disciplines and care deeply about helping public sector organizations deploy advanced AI safely and responsibly.         About OpenAI   OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.
